children.title: Cost Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Solution response to changes in edge or assignment costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation bounds for the minimum-cost value with a fixed feasible-flow polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^E\) be a nonempty bounded flow polytope fixed by capacities and supplies, and define \(V(c)=\min_{x\in P}c^{\mathsf T}x\). For a cost perturbation \(d\), choose \(x\in\arg\min_{y\in P}c^{\mathsf T}y\) and \(x'\in\arg\min_{y\in P}(c+d)^{\mathsf T}y\). Then \[d^{\mathsf T}x'\le V(c+d)-V(c)\le d^{\mathsf T}x.\] Consequently, if \(0\le x_e\le u_e\), then \(|V(c+d)-V(c)|\le\sum_{e\in E}u_e|d_e|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing arc costs changes the optimum between the perturbation evaluated at the old and new optimal flows, yielding a capacity-weighted Lipschitz bound.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is nonempty and bounded.
The perturbation changes costs only; capacities and supplies remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^{\mathsf T}x'\le V(c+d)-V(c)\le d^{\mathsf T}x\).

notation.meaning: minimum flow cost under cost vector c

children.title: Capacity Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity and optimizer preservation under capacity perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed arc costs \(c\) and node supplies \(b\), let \(P(u)=\{x:Bx=b,\ 0\le x\le u\}\) and \(V(u)=\min_{x\in P(u)}c^{\mathsf T}x\), with \(V(u)=+\infty\) when \(P(u)=\varnothing\). If \(u'\ge u\) componentwise, then \(P(u)\subseteq P(u')\) and \(V(u')\le V(u)\). If \(u'\le u\) componentwise and some optimizer \(x\in P(u)\) also satisfies \(x\le u'\), then \(x\in P(u')\), remains optimal for \(u'\), and \(V(u')=V(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing capacities enlarges the feasible set and cannot increase minimum cost. Under a capacity decrease, an old optimum remains optimal and the value is unchanged whenever that optimum remains feasible.
assumptions_latex: Arc costs and node supplies remain fixed.
Capacities are finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u'\ge u\Rightarrow V(u')\le V(u)\); if \(u'\le u\) and an optimizer for \(u\) remains feasible, then \(V(u')=V(u)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Supply Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual subgradient bound for perturbations of balanced node supplies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix costs and capacities, and let \(V(b)\) be the minimum cost of a flow satisfying \(Bx=b\) and \(0\le x\le u\). Suppose \(b\) and \(b'\) are balanced and feasible. If \(\pi\) is the node-potential component of an optimal dual solution for supply vector \(b\), with the dual objective written so that its supply term is \(b^{\mathsf T}\pi\), then weak duality at \(b'\) gives \[V(b')\ge V(b)+\pi^{\mathsf T}(b'-b).\] Equality holds when the same dual solution is optimal for \(b'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal node-potential vector gives a linear lower bound on how minimum cost changes when balanced node supplies are perturbed.
assumptions_latex: \(b\) and \(b'\) satisfy \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}b=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}b'=0\).
Both perturbed flow problems are feasible and attain their optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(b')-V(b)\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(b'-b)\).

children.title: Potential-Based Reoptimization

knowledge_statements.title: Potential-Based Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost optimality certificate reusable after a network update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible capacitated flow \(x\) and node potential vector \(\pi\), assign each residual arc \((i,j)\) the reduced cost \(\bar c_{ij}=c_{ij}+\pi_i-\pi_j\), with a reverse residual arc carrying the negative of its corresponding original arc cost. The condition \(\bar c_{ij}\ge0\) for every residual arc is an optimality certificate for \(x\). After an update for which \(x\) remains feasible, a retained potential vector \(\pi\) permits the certificate to be checked on residual arcs newly created or modified by the update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative reduced costs on all residual arcs certify optimality; a retained potential vector allows the certificate to be checked again after an update.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is feasible for the updated capacitated minimum-cost flow instance.
Reverse residual arcs carry the negatives of their corresponding original arc costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_{ij}\ge0\) on every residual arc implies that \(x\) is minimum-cost.

children.title: Dual-Based Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Reuse or repair of broader dual solution information after instance changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Based Reoptimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-start principle based on retained dual feasibility and the primal–dual gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an updated minimum-cost flow linear program with primal objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) and dual objective \(D(y)\). If a dual solution \(y\) retained from the previous instance remains feasible after the update, then \(D(y)\) is a valid lower bound on the new optimum. For any repaired primal-feasible flow \(x\), the computable gap \(c^{\mathsf T}x-D(y)\) is nonnegative and bounds the primal suboptimality. Reoptimization may therefore begin from \(y\), repairing only violated dual constraints; simultaneous primal repair terminates with an exact optimum when feasibility holds on both sides and the gap is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retained feasible dual solution supplies a lower bound and a measurable gap, allowing reoptimization to focus on newly violated dual constraints.
assumptions_latex: The updated primal and dual programs satisfy strong duality.
The retained dual variables have the same interpretation in the updated formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le c^{\mathsf T}x-V^*\le c^{\mathsf T}x-D(y)\), with equality to zero certifying optimality.

children.title: Primal–Dual Repair Interface
children.top_down_role: Interaction between repaired dual information and restoration of primal flow or assignment solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Repair Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping and certification conditions for a primal–dual repair interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an updated minimum-cost flow instance, let \(x\) be a primal candidate, let \(y\) be a dual candidate, and define the primal–dual gap by \(g=c^{\mathsf T}x-D(y)\) whenever both candidates are feasible. A primal–dual repair interface may return \(x\) as an exact solution when primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and \(g=0\) all hold. For a prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), it may return a primal-feasible \(x\) with additive suboptimality at most \(\varepsilon\) when \(y\) is dual feasible and \(0\le g\le\varepsilon\). These conditions certify returned solutions but do not by themselves guarantee that a particular sequence of repairs terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal–dual repair interface may stop exactly when both candidates are feasible and their gap is zero, or approximately when the feasible gap is at most the prescribed additive tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The updated primal and dual formulations satisfy strong duality when feasible.
\(D(y)\) is the dual objective corresponding to the primal objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x\).
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility on both sides with \(g=0\) certifies exact optimality; feasibility on both sides with \(0\le g\le\varepsilon\) certifies additive error at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Minimum-Cost Flow Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exact maintenance of a capacitated minimum-cost flow under parameter updates on a fixed ambient network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a fixed ambient set of directed arcs with incidence matrix \(B\). At update time \(k\), let \(c_k\in\mathbb{R}^{E}\), \(u_k\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{E}\), and balanced supplies \(b_k\) define the current instance. Dynamic minimum-cost flow maintenance processes changes to \(c_k\), \(u_k\), or \(b_k\) and, after every update, either reports infeasibility or returns \(x_k\) satisfying \(Bx_k=b_k\), \(0\le x_k\le u_k\), and \[c_k^{\mathsf T}x_k=\min\{c_k^{\mathsf T}x:Bx=b_k,\ 0\le x\le u_k\}.\] Within the fixed ambient arc set, activating an arc is represented by changing its capacity from zero to a positive value, and deleting an arc is represented by setting its capacity to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After each cost, capacity, supply, arc-activation, or arc-deactivation update on a fixed ambient network, maintain an optimal feasible minimum-cost flow or report infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}b_k=0\) for every update time \(k\).
Costs and capacities are finite, with \(u_k\ge0\).
The ambient arc set \(E\) and incidence matrix \(B\) remain fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic Assignment Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines exact minimum-cost perfect-assignment maintenance under bipartite updates.

children.title: Amortized Update Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Dynamic performance guarantees averaged across update sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Amortized Update Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard aggregate-cost definition for a dynamic algorithm over a legal update sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an initial instance of size \(n_0\) undergo a legal sequence \(\sigma=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\), and let \(c_i\ge 0\) be the work performed while processing \(u_i\). The algorithm has amortized update time \(T\) with preprocessing allowance \(P\) if, for every \(\sigma\), \[\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i\le P(n_0)+mT(n_0,m).\] For a randomized algorithm against an oblivious adversary, an expected amortized guarantee instead requires the same inequality after applying \(\mathbb E_R\), for every fixed sequence \(\sigma\) independent of the random seed \(R\). The definition permits individual updates to cost more than \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Amortized update time bounds total work over every legal update sequence; individual updates may exceed the stated per-update average.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma=(u_1,\ldots,u_m)\) is a legal update sequence.
Each update has a nonnegative processing cost \(c_i\).

notation.meaning: work used to process update i

children.title: Worst-Case Update Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Dynamic performance guarantees applying to every individual update.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Update Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-operation update guarantee, distinguished from an aggregate amortized bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every legal update history \(h_{i-1}=(u_1,\ldots,u_{i-1})\), let \(n_i\) be the current instance size and let \(c_i\) be the work used for the next legal update \(u_i\). A deterministic dynamic algorithm has worst-case update time \(T\) if \[c_i\le T(n_i)\] for every index \(i\), history \(h_{i-1}\), and permitted \(u_i\). A high-probability randomized version must state its quantifiers explicitly; against an oblivious sequence \(\sigma\), one standard form is \(\Pr_R[\max_{1\le i\le m}c_i\le T(n_i)]\ge 1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case update time bounds every individual update on every legal history, rather than merely bounding their aggregate cost.

children.title: Deamortization Separations
children.top_down_role: Gaps and boundaries between amortized performance and attainable per-update performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Deamortization Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract separation showing that an amortized guarantee alone has no worst-case consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a phase length \(n\). Consider a correct dynamic maintenance procedure whose phase contains \(n\) updates and whose deferred maintenance performs no charged work on the first \(n-1\) updates and \(n\) work units on the final update. Its phase cost is \(n\), so its amortized update cost is \(n/n=1\), while its worst-case update cost is \(n\). Consequently, an aggregate bound \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}c_i=O(m)\) does not imply \(\max_i c_i=O(1)\). A deamortization theorem therefore requires additional structure enabling deferred work to be scheduled incrementally while preserving correctness and space bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear total work can hide a linear-cost update, so an amortized bound cannot by itself be converted into the same worst-case bound.
assumptions_latex: Maintenance work may be deferred within a phase of \(n\) updates.
Correct answers remain available while the deferred maintenance is pending.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}c_i=1\) while \(\max_{1\le i\le n}c_i=n\)

notation.meaning: number of updates in one phase
maintenance work charged to update i

knowledge_statements.title: Cell-Probe Dynamic Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic lower bounds in the cell-probe model with free computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the dynamic cell-probe model, memory consists of cells containing \(w\) bits each; all computation is free, and cost is the number of cell reads and writes. For a dynamic problem \(\Pi\), a lower bound \(L(n,w)\) on worst-case operation time means that every data structure solving \(\Pi\) with the stipulated error probability has some legal operation sequence and some operation on which at least \(L(n,w)\) cells are probed. A tradeoff lower bound is a predicate such as \(F(t_u,t_q,n,w)\ge 0\), required of every admissible structure with update time \(t_u\) and query time \(t_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dynamic cell-probe lower bound counts necessary memory-cell accesses while treating computation as free, often expressing an update–query tradeoff.
assumptions_latex: Each memory cell contains exactly \(w\) bits.
The success criterion and whether costs are worst-case or amortized are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(t_u,t_q,n,w)\ge 0\) for every admissible data structure

knowledge_statements.title: Online Matrix–Vector Conditional Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic OMv reduction template; concrete dynamic tradeoffs depend on the target problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The OMv conjecture asserts that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), no randomized algorithm with error at most \(1/3\), after polynomial preprocessing of an \(n\times n\) Boolean matrix \(M\), can receive \(n\) Boolean vectors online and output every Boolean product \(Mv_i\) before seeing \(v_{i+1}\) in total time \(O(n^{3-\varepsilon})\). Hence, if a reduction uses a dynamic data structure to solve OMv in time \[P(N)+a(n)U(N)+b(n)Q(N)+R(n),\] then, conditionally on OMv, this expression cannot be \(O(n^{3-\varepsilon})\), where \(P,U,Q\) are preprocessing, update, and query costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An OMv reduction forbids dynamic preprocessing, update, and query bounds whose combined simulated running time would be truly subcubic.
assumptions_latex: The OMv conjecture holds for randomized algorithms with error at most \(1/3\).
The reduction preserves online output order and the stated error bound.
The reduction performs \(a(n)\) updates and \(b(n)\) queries on instances of size \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(N)+a(n)U(N)+b(n)Q(N)+R(n)\ne O(n^{3-\varepsilon})\) for every applicable \(\varepsilon>0\)

knowledge_statements.title: Fine-Grained Conditional Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction-based transfer of a fine-grained conjecture to a dynamic time tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a source problem on size \(n\) be conjectured not to admit time \(O(S(n)^{1-\varepsilon})\) for any \(\varepsilon>0\). Suppose a reduction, using a dynamic data structure on instances of size \(N(n)\), solves the source problem with \(a(n)\) updates, \(b(n)\) queries, preprocessing cost \(P(N(n))\), and additional work \(R(n)\). Then the conjecture conditionally requires \[P(N(n))+a(n)U(N(n))+b(n)Q(N(n))+R(n)\ne O(S(n)^{1-\varepsilon}).\] The resulting barrier applies only under the reduction's computation model, error regime, and preprocessing assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fine-grained reduction excludes dynamic bounds that would combine into an algorithm violating the source problem's conjectured running-time barrier.

children.title: Adaptive-Adversary Failures
children.top_down_role: Failure modes caused by update choices that depend on observed algorithm behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Adversary Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier separation between fixed-sequence randomness and transcript-adaptive updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the random seed \(R\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,N\}\), and suppose an observable answer reveals \(R\). For each \(j\), let \(u_j\) be a legal next update causing failure exactly when \(R=j\). For every fixed, seed-independent update \(u_j\), \(\Pr_R[\mathrm{failure\ on\ }u_j]=1/N\). An adaptive adversary first observes the revealing answer and then submits \(u_R\), yielding \(\Pr_R[\mathrm{failure}]=1\). Thus a guarantee quantified over every fixed oblivious sequence does not imply the corresponding guarantee against an adversary whose next update depends on the observed transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A seed-independent update fails rarely, yet an adversary that learns the seed from outputs can select an update that fails surely.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm exposes an answer from which its seed \(R\) can be identified.
Every update \(u_j\) is legal after the revealing answer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall j,\ \Pr_R[\mathrm{failure\ on\ }u_j]=1/N\), but \(\Pr_R[\mathrm{failure\ on\ }u_R]=1\)

notation.meaning: update tailored to seed value j

children.title: Randomness-Robustness Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdowns of probabilistic guarantees under exposure, dependence, or insufficient randomness.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomness-Robustness Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected update cost does not furnish a uniform tail or worst-case guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each update, let a randomized algorithm incur cost \(C=N\) with probability \(1/N\) and cost \(C=0\) otherwise. Then \(\mathbb E[C]=1\), so the expected update cost is constant, but \(\Pr[C>N/2]=1/N\) and the worst-case cost is \(N\). Over \(m\) independent updates, the probability that at least one update costs \(N\) is \(1-(1-1/N)^m\). Therefore an expected-time guarantee alone cannot certify a smaller failure probability, a simultaneous high-probability bound over the operation sequence, or a deterministic worst-case bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant expected update cost can hide rare linear-cost updates, which accumulate substantial failure probability over a long sequence.
assumptions_latex: The update-cost draws are independent when the multi-update probability is evaluated.
\(N\ge 2\) and \(m\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[C]=1\) while \(\Pr[\max_{1\le i\le m}C_i=N]=1-(1-1/N)^m\)

notation.meaning: rare high-cost magnitude and inverse event probability

children.title: Oblivious-Adversary Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits separating guarantees for fixed update sequences from guarantees against adaptive choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Oblivious-Adversary Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precommitment condition delimiting guarantees proved only for obliviously selected operation sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\) be the algorithm's internal random seed and let \(A\) denote any private randomness used by the adversary, with \(A\) independent of \(R\). An adversary is oblivious when it selects the complete legal operation sequence \(\Sigma=f(A)\) before execution, without observing \(R\) or any execution transcript. Thus \(\Sigma\) is independent of \(R\), although outputs produced during execution may depend on both \(R\) and \(\Sigma\). A high-probability oblivious-adversary guarantee has the form \[\forall \sigma\in\mathcal S,\qquad \Pr_R[G(R,\sigma)]\ge 1-\delta,\] where \(\mathcal S\) is the set of legal fixed sequences. This quantifier form does not cover a sequence whose later operations are selected from outputs observed earlier in the same execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oblivious adversary commits to the complete legal operation sequence before execution, without observing the algorithm's seed or transcript; transcript-dependent later operations are adaptive and lie outside the guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal S\) is a specified set of legal fixed operation sequences.
The adversary's private randomness \(A\), if any, is independent of the algorithm's internal seed \(R\).
Probability in the displayed guarantee is taken over \(R\) for each fixed \(\sigma\in\mathcal S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall \sigma\in\mathcal S,\ \Pr_R[G(R,\sigma)]\ge 1-\delta\)

notation.meaning: adversary's private randomness, independent of R
complete operation sequence committed to before execution

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard precommitment and quantifier characterization of an oblivious adversary
